accessDecisions.name: Pine River Cross Lake Below-dam Carry-in
accessDecisions.note: The original DNR point identifies the below-dam access area. Trees and snow obscure the exact landing; retain an Area marker. The map labels the broader recreation facility left-bank, while the inventory locates this below-dam carry-in on the west/right bank; no verified bank badge assigned.

accessDecisions.name: Pine River Staircase Carry-in
accessDecisions.note: DNR confirms a natural carry-in at river mile 18.5. The original point sits by the wooded bank and approach; the precise stairs and water edge are obscured. Retain the source coordinate as an Area marker.

accessDecisions.name: Pine River Rock Dam Below-rapids Carry-in
accessDecisions.note: DNR recommends starting below Rock Dam. Its facility coordinate is beside the upper constructed rapids, not a confirmed downstream landing. Preserve it as an approximate facility area and leave the landing connection unmapped. This site has blank water-trail join fields and is included in the source import by stable ID.

accessDecisions.name: Pine River Harvey Drake Landing
accessDecisions.note: Unchanged DNR GPS coordinate matches the shoreline end of the visible ramp approach immediately upstream of the County Road 11 bridge. DNR lists a concrete trailer launch, and its 2026 map independently places Harvey Drake on river right at mile 0.9. Desktop agency and imagery review, not a field survey; water level and ramp conditions may change.

courseObservations: Parts 1–2: Cross Lake below-dam start, Staircase bend and Gould/Anton reaches follow the connected visible river; minor bank generalization retained.

Parts 3–4: source crosses the widened impoundment and depicts the western channel through the Rock Dam structure. No navigation passage through that structure is approved; rapid notices remain on crossing trips.
Parts 5–8: continuous main river bends match the visible channel; no shortcuts across forest or disconnected oxbows.
Parts 9–10: line stays on the Pine River at the Little Pine confluence rather than following the tributary.
Parts 11–12: lower bends remain connected; course ends beside Harvey Drake upstream of the County Road 11 bridge.
Rock Dam below-rapids trip begins at original source vertex 521, 141.5 m from the general facility point and below the visible structure. Exact carry-in connection is omitted.
All source vertices are preserved within each explicitly trimmed reach. Imagery checks establish an approximate planning overview, not present-day navigability or a field-surveyed channel.

acceptedIssues.endpoint-offset-over-100m: Intentional downstream trim below Rock Dam rapids; the original agency facility coordinate remains an Area marker. No invented landing connector.

rockDamTrim.reason: Begin the displayed below-rapids course at existing source vertex 521, downstream of the constructed weirs and split channels. The facility coordinate remains unchanged; the carry-in connection is not mapped.

distanceDecision: DNR river miles decrease downstream: Cross Lake carry-in 19.8, Staircase 18.5, Rock Dam 15.3, Harvey Drake 0.9. Published planning miles stay separate from source-line length and the omitted Rock Dam approach.

gaugeDecision.note: USACE outflow exists outside the app supported adapters. No stand-in upstream gauge, flow-speed calibration or GPS remaining-time feature enabled.

guideTimeDecision: Crow Wing Kayaks route 12 matches Rock Dam–Harvey Drake and publishes 6+ hours; represent max explicitly as null. Route 10 matches Cross Lake–Harvey Drake and gives approximately 8 hours. Do not transfer durations from different endpoints or convert DNR full-day wording into a numeric estimate.
sourceImportDecision: DNR Rock Dam site WAS02986 has blank water-trail ID/name fields. Add that stable ID as a documented query exception; complete refresh adds one feature, removes none and changes none. Discovery does not automatically verify coordinates.

heldAccessLeads.name: Pine River Snowmobile Trail take-out
heldAccessLeads.reason: Crow Wing Kayaks identifies a popular 4.5-mile Rock Dam trip ending here, but the consulted DNR water-trail access inventory does not establish a distinct landing and public approach.
heldAccessLeads.nextAction: Find managing-agency or county evidence of the exact site identity, public boating access, approach and coordinates. Preserve the outfitter trip as a research lead; do not invent a ramp from the trail crossing.
